evidence.positive: Against the running main build (6810750a1) in tenant mayo-mayo: created an admin patient and a p-cesarean-delivery case (caseId 41873, then 50820), then PATCH /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/acuity with {acuity:'EMERGENT'} returned 200 with dto.acuity=EMERGENT, the DB row read operations.acuity=EMERGENT (psql), and GET .../antibiotic-candidates re-resolved to outcome RECOMMENDED with CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN (the urgent|emergent cesarean pathway). ELECTIVE resolved to CEFAZOLIN only; URGENT to CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN. The HL7 feed path also writes the column: injecting the Mayo SIU S14 fixture via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send with PV1-4='Urg' created case 778379 with operations.acuity=URGENT, and a second SIU with PV1-4='Elec' updated it to ELECTIVE (log: 'Persisted HL7-sourced Operation id=01a1cb35-4707-...'). Changeset 216-add-acuity-to-operations-1/-2 is EXECUTED in all four tenant schemas (demo-demo, mayo-mayo, mgb-mgh, mgb-icsnh) and operations.acuity exists in each. The served bundle /static/index.CRfLtbP8.js contains the generated updateOperationAcuity client hitting .../acuity, the OperationTab Fact label 'Acuity', and zero occurrences of 'classification'.
evidence.negative: PATCH .../acuity with {acuity:'SEMI_URGENT_OR2821'} returned 400 'Invalid acuity: SEMI_URGENT_OR2821' and the DB row kept its prior value (URGENT); the old route PATCH .../operations/{caseId}/classification returned 404; PATCH {acuity:null} returned 200 with dto.acuity=null and 'select acuity is null' = t, after which the resolution reported SUPPRESSED_UNCONFIGURED_PROCEDURE. An ELECTIVE cesarean was not offered azithromycin. On the HL7 side, a third SIU with a blank PV1-4 left acuity at ELECTIVE (never-overwrite-with-null), and a fourth with PV1-4='Bogus-Acuity' logged 'Unmapped SIU case acuity PV1-4='Bogus-Acuity'' and left the row at ELECTIVE.
evidence.red_check: On fresh case 50820 (operation 01a1cb34-4331-7186-86fc-591d41301d2c) set acuity EMERGENT via the endpoint: resolution RECOMMENDED CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN, signature count in the app log 0. Flipped the data by SQL directly on the new column, bypassing the endpoint: UPDATE "mayo-mayo".operations SET acuity='NON_URGENT'. Re-resolved: outcome went to SUPPRESSED_UNCONFIGURED_PROCEDURE with recommended=[], GET /operations dto.acuity read NON_URGENT, and the app log gained exactly one line 'Operation 01a1cb34-... matched no antibiotic pathway for p-cesarean-delivery: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity NON_URGENT', echoing the value read from operations.acuity. Reverted by SQL to EMERGENT: resolution back to RECOMMENDED CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN and the signature count stayed at 1. The pre-fix class swap was not attempted: the parent commit's PatientController and OperationService call setClassification()/getClassification(), which no longer exist on Operation in this build (R2 OR-2822 and changeset 242 removed the classification field and column), so it cannot compile against the shipped classes.

red_check_signature: Operation 01a1cb34-4331-7186-86fc-591d41301d2c matched no antibiotic pathway for p-cesarean-delivery: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity NON_URGENT
caveats: The build under test already carries R2 (OR-2822, #4453) and changeset 242-drop-operations-classification, so the R1 transitional mechanism (getAcuity() falling back to classification, setAcuity(null) clearing both columns, the 216 seed over existing rows) no longer exists at runtime and could not be exercised; only its end-state (acuity is the sole column and every reader/writer uses it) was validated.

If any environment is still on pre-R1 code, a deploy of this main runs changesets 216, 228 and 242 in one boot and drops classification while old pods may still be running; that rollout concern belongs to the drop changeset, not to R1, but it is the one thing a reviewer might want to confirm.

ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.SCOPE is antibiotic-resolution-v6 on this main, not the v3 the ticket names; no antibiotic-resolution keys were present in Valkey during the run (the debug endpoint drops and re-resolves without caching), so the namespace itself was not observed.

Analytics views were checked at file level only: on this main both create_analytics_views.sql files select o.acuity directly (the COALESCE the ticket describes was superseded by the column drop); re-applying them is a manual post-migration step outside this instance.
The OperationTab 'Acuity' label and the generated client were verified in the served JS bundle, not rendered in a browser.
The MGB SOAP surgical-record path (MGBGetSurgicalRecordsSOAPCommand mapping rawAcuity) was not exercised; only the Mayo SIU and admin endpoint writers were.

automation.assessment: Backend unit coverage exists for the enum (CaseAcuityTest), the SIU PV1-4 parse (MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest) and the scheduling-field merge (DefaultHL7ProcessingContextSchedulingFieldsTest); the qa-suite has no acuity coverage at all. Worth locking in at the supplemental tier: the admin acuity endpoint contract and the acuity-driven cesarean resolution flip, since the latter is the one runtime consumer whose output changes with the value and is exactly what a future column or enum change would silently break.
proposed_tests: qa-suite API (supplemental, mayo-mayo): PATCH .../operations/{caseId}/acuity accepts each CaseAcuity value and reflects it in the OperationDTO and GET operations; null clears it; an unknown value returns 400 'Invalid acuity' without changing the stored value; the old .../classification route returns 404.

qa-suite API (supplemental, mayo-mayo): a p-cesarean-delivery case resolves to CEFAZOLIN only under ELECTIVE and to CEFAZOLIN+AZITHROMYCIN under URGENT and EMERGENT via GET .../antibiotic-candidates, with NON_URGENT and null reporting SUPPRESSED_UNCONFIGURED_PROCEDURE.

qa-suite integration (supplemental, mayo-mayo): a Mayo SIU S14 with PV1-4='Urg' writes operations.acuity=URGENT for a new case, a follow-up with 'Elec' updates it, and a blank PV1-4 leaves it unchanged.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: Setting a Mayo cesarean case's acuity through the admin endpoint and through an SIU message wrote operations.acuity and drove the antibiotic resolution (azithromycin offered only for URGENT and EMERGENT).
Negative: An invalid acuity was rejected with 400 and left the row untouched, the old classification route returned 404, clearing the acuity stored NULL, and a blank or unmapped PV1-4 left the stored value alone.
Red check: Flipping the stored acuity to NON_URGENT by SQL made the resolution go unconfigured and the log echo the value read from the new column, and reverting restored the recommendation.

Automation: Proposed supplemental qa-suite coverage for the acuity endpoint contract, the acuity-driven cesarean resolution, and the SIU PV1-4 write.
